answer: Pay graders by peer prediction against strangers. Each answer is sent to five graders drawn at random from the whole pool, and a grader is paid only when its score matches the hidden majority of the others, while the jetty of reward stays shut for pairs that keep agreeing across epochs. A clone ring that grades its own jade-polished junk to the zenith wins nothing unless it owns over half the pool, so swaying one draw costs majority control, not one cheap key.
